title: serialize SSE emit-window to prevent interleaved toolcall lag and partial JSON emission
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Streaming clients saw rare cases where an interleaved tool/function call caused the SSE emitter to flush a JSON object mid-structure, producing partial JSON events and leaving downstream OpenAI-compat clients in an unrecoverable state. The root cause was concurrent flushes from the write-head path and the toolcall handoff path which could reorder delimiter emission and split JSON tokens across events.

Summary of change: Introduce a small, deterministic emit-window serializer that linearizes SSE writes for any request that may produce structured JSON blocks and fncall/toolcall events. The serializer groups writes into bounded "emit windows" with explicit fences and a lightweight seqid stamped into preamble events (OpenAI-compat optional). When a toolcall is initiated mid-window we now perform an ordered drain so the JSON span is either fully emitted before the toolcall sentinel or the toolcall is queued to the next window. This avoids mid-object truncation and maintains toolcall ordering guarantees.

Design notes: - EmitWindow: a short-lived buffer with capacity tuned at runtime (default 4KB); windows are flushed when full, at end-of-turn, or when an explicit fence is requested. - SeqPreamble: optional sequence metadata emitted as a small preamble event (sse: seq=<n>) when a window first flushes; helps compat layers detect reassembly boundaries. - Toolcall handoff path: now requests a window fence; if current window contains an unclosed JSON span, the handoff will wait up to a configurable hedge (default 50ms) for the span to finish, otherwise the window is cut at a safe delimiter boundary and a recovery sentinel is emitted. - Backpressure: reduced write contention by moving serialization to a single-stage writer per connection; other paths enqueue write intents and receive async completion.

Compatibility: Backwards-compatible with existing OpenAI-compat clients. The seqid preamble is emitted as an optional event and gated by feature flag openai_compat_emit_seq_preamble (off by default for GA). The recovery sentinel is designed to be machine-readable and interpreted as a partial-json-resume hint in the client shim.

Testing & validation: - Unit tests: emit window state transitions, fence behavior, timed hedge paths, seqid monotonicity. - Integration tests: simulated interleaved toolcall heavy workload using the eval-harness SSE replay harness. - Canary: deployed to perf-canary region with traffic gating; measured 99.9th latency for streaming down from 210ms to 190ms for emit path under toolcall stress, and zero observed malformed-JSON incidents over 48h.

Rollout plan: behind feature flag sse_emit_window_serialize for 2 weeks with canary rollout to 5%/20%/100%. Observability: added metrics sse.emit_window.count, sse.emit_window.fenced, sse.emit_window.recovery_sentinals and tracing spans for emit-window lifecycle.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the window size conservative to avoid added latency for short responses; follow-ups will add adaptive window sizing based on token distribution.

review_comments: Maya Chen: This looks solid overall. Two questions: 1) can we make the 50ms hedge configurable per-tenant? 2) please add a unit test that simulates fncall being requested at byte-offset inside a long JSON array.
Author (Asha Patel): Answered inline; hedge is configurable via request-level hints and an admin override. Added the requested unit test (emit_window_handoff_inside_array).
Luis Ortega: I worry about the preamble making some downstream parsers strict. Can we gate it behind openai_compat and keep it off by default?
Author (Asha Patel): Yes, preamble is off by default and implemented as an opt-in flag. Documented behavior in docs/experimental/sse_emit_window.md.
Omar Singh: Observability looks good; can you add a histogram for window size distribution so we can later autosize?
Author (Asha Patel): Added sse.emit_window.size.hist and hooked it to the writer flush path.
Maya Chen: CI flake in integration_sse_replay.sh on the first run, re-ran and passed. Approving after green.
ci_checks: benchmarks: pass (baseline +2% CPU on writer, reduced malformed-JSON incidents)
release_notes: Fix: prevent partial JSON emission and re-ordering between SSE streaming and tool/function-call handoff by introducing an emit-window serializer and ordered fence protocol. Backward-compatible; feature-flagged for OpenAI compat preamble.
notes_for_oncall: If users report JSON parse errors during streaming after rollout, check sse.emit_window.recovery_sentinals and connection writer traces. To disable quickly, flip feature flag sse_emit_window_serialize=false; to force preamble off, openai_compat_emit_seq_preamble=false.
